🧠 Crypto News Brief: An active Coldcard wallet exploit and a stalling CLARITY Act have crypto on edge — yet Bitcoin holds near $63.8K with volatility at multi-month lows, as "extreme fear" grips sentiment more than price. 🔓 Coldcard exploit still draining wallets, losses near $114M Coldcard's developers issued an urgent warning on Tuesday telling users to move their bitcoin, as a firmware flaw dormant since 2021 keeps letting attackers guess weakly randomized seed keys. Galaxy Research now flags a possible fourth wave, lifting cumulative losses from roughly $89 million toward $114 million across thousands of self-custodied addresses. Wallets set up using the dice-roll option are considered safe. Read full story → 🏛️ CLARITY Act on a knife-edge as Senate recess looms The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act faces a make-or-break window, with only days left before senators leave Washington for their August break. The bill has cleared the House and the Senate Banking Committee but still needs 60 floor votes, and no cloture motion or floor vote has been scheduled. Prediction markets have trimmed the odds of passage this year. More details → 📈 Spot Bitcoin ETFs pull in $170M as Ether funds slip US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded roughly $170.1 million of net inflows on August 3, underscoring steady institutional appetite for BTC. Spot Ether ETFs, by contrast, logged an $11.9 million net outflow, snapping a two-day inflow streak and highlighting cooler momentum for Ethereum products, according to Farside data. See details → 🏦 Strategy trims Bitcoin as Bitmine keeps stacking Ether Strategy, the largest corporate bitcoin holder, disclosed another sale — about 1,638 BTC worth roughly $105 million — alongside buybacks of its preferred stock and fresh equity raises. Meanwhile, Tom Lee's Bitmine added 10,399 ETH last week, pushing its treasury near 5.8 million ether, about 4.8% of circulating supply, and citing Ethereum's July outperformance versus the Nasdaq. Read more → 😨 Bitcoin stays eerily calm as "extreme fear" takes hold Despite the Coldcard exploit, soft institutional demand and macro uncertainty, Bitcoin is hovering near $63,800 with its 30-day implied volatility gauge sliding to its lowest since late May.
